text.p: The following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:
- Prime Minister-designate Janez Drnovsek, who has to present his government lineup to parliament by Friday, has not yet managed to form a coalition.
- January pensions were up by 1.9 percent, the Slovenian Pension Fund said.
- Negotiators of the states of the former Yugoslavia, who started a two-day meeting in Brussels on Wednesday to debate succession issues, reached no result as yet.
- A Slovenian basketball team Smelt Olimpija won a EuroLeague match with Russia's Dinamo in Moscow on Wednesday by 76 against 64.
- The government prepared a bill according to which all casinos would remain in state property. The bill has yet to be passed by parliament.
- Slovenian skiing resorts said they had more visitors in January and December than in the same period of the last year.
- Since 1994 Slovenian schools invested 2.1 billion tolars ($14 million) in computer education, the Education Ministry said.
- NATO sources said Slovenia was one of the strongest candidates for full membership in NATO.
